label: World population
note: Peaks mid-2040s, decades earlier than the UN median (WPP 2024: 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s), because the forecast bets fertility falls faster than the UN assumes nearly everywhere. The observed points are the UN's.

label: Life expectancy, rich countries
note: Median of the G7 plus Australia, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland (2023: 83, from Japan 84.7 to the US 79.3). Flat for a decade, then climbs once aging therapies clear approval. Under concentration the therapies exist but reach fewer people, so the median rises slower.

label: Cognitive work done by AI
note: Share of measurable knowledge-work output produced by or with AI systems. Concentration gets there slightly faster because one actor deploys without competition.

label: Full-time paid hours a week
note: A rich-country full-time schedule, not the all-worker average (OECD average actual hours were 33.4 a week in 2025, including part-time). Under pluralism the drop is negotiated (shorter weeks, income floors); under concentration it is faster and mostly involuntary.

label: Warming above pre-industrial
note: 1.5°C missed in the late 2020s; 2°C breached around 2050; peak and slow decline after as emissions fall and removal scales.

label: Humans living off-Earth
note: Nearly all in orbit or on the Moon through 2100. A single dominant actor builds faster off-Earth; pluralism spreads effort thinner.

label: Actors at the AI frontier
note: Organizations or states able to train and deploy systems within a year of the best. Counted from Epoch's capability index: about ten in 2026 (five US labs, five Chinese labs within four to seven months). A judgment count, not a published series. The hinge, as a number.
